lede:
Forty-two takes. Every one of them failed in one of three ways, and laid out together they are not three problems — they are one problem I kept solving in the wrong direction.

What has actually been tried
briefwhat was in the framehow it failed
first, 18 takesthe weapon, alonehandguns — an object at no scale
second, 12 takesthe weapon + a huge foreground hull + a distant shipthe big hull became the subject
third, 12 takesthe rounds, alonedisembodied missiles — your word, and your original diagnosis
this onethe rounds + a small distant ship, and nothing in the foregrounduntried

Each time I removed whatever broke the last attempt, and twice I removed the wrong thing. The distant ship was never the problem — the huge foreground hull was. I threw out both, and what was left had nothing to be about.

So: keep the target, drop the hull. Something is being shot at, it is small and far away because that is what makes the rounds read as huge, and there is nothing near the camera to steal the frame. That is the only combination of the four that has never been in front of you. If it fails too, this card should take its glyph and I will stop spending your afternoon on it.

cards.actor: three rounds in flight, strung out along one line
cards.on: a small ship in the distance that they are converging on, still whole, still unhit
cards.moment: the near round large and cut by the frame edge, the second smaller behind it, the third a bright point far off — and at the end of that line, small, a ship that has not been hit yet. The gaps between the rounds are the rate of fire. The ship is what makes it an attack rather than three objects drifting.
cards.scale: the size difference between the near round and the far ship does all of it. Nothing else is needed and nothing else is allowed near the camera — a foreground structure is exactly what took the frame over last time.
cards.avoid: any large ship, any ship in the foreground, any gun, mount or muzzle, and nothing at all between the camera and the nearest round. The target stays SMALL and FAR: it is what is being shot at, not what the picture is of. In the prompt, no 'hull', no 'vessel', no 'shell' — all three have imported an ocean or a floor with no other prompting.
